lines.trans: I drank way too much yesterday.
Your wretched drinking habit of blacking out every time you touch alcohol—thank you so much, Joon-mo!
Once you walked us home, you should have gone home to sleep too—why did you sleep here?
Hey, why are you in here?
Because I was escorting you seniors home last night.
Hey, what is my apartment—a motel or the station night-duty room?
I worked so hard to talk my parents into getting this place so I could enjoy a free single life alone…
so how on earth does the headcount keep growing!
Wait—is this not your first time sleeping over at this apartment?
It has turned into a full-blown boarding house!

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this yesterday?
I was busy today because of yesterday.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.
I want to drink right now.
How about trying to drink together tomorrow?
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Native Korean expression of thanks; 고마워요 is warm and polite.

examples.trans: Thank you so much for helping me.
Thank you always.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Once you walked us home, you should have gone home to sleep too—why did you sleep here?

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 주다, used when giving to elders or superiors.

examples.trans: I gave a present to my grandmother.
May I ask you a question?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Did you sleep well last night?
The baby is sleeping right now.

related.gloss: to wake up; to get up

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Casual exclamation used to call someone younger or a close friend.

examples.trans: Hey, come quickly!
Hey, where are you going?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

examples.trans: This is my bag.
